exam.q: 'Religious believers should accept same-sex marriage.' Evaluate this statement. In your answer you: should give reasoned arguments in support of this statement; should give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view; should refer to religious arguments; may refer to non-religious arguments; should reach a justified conclusion.
exam.model:
Some religious believers agree with this statement. Quakers, the Methodist Church, the United Reformed Church and Reform and Liberal Jews all hold same-sex weddings. They argue that 'God is love' (1 John 4:8) and that every person is made in God's image (Genesis 1:27), so a loving, faithful, lifelong commitment between two people of the same sex reflects God's love just as much as any other marriage. They also say Jesus never mentioned same-sex relationships but taught love of neighbour, and that the verses used against them were about exploitation in ancient cultures. This is a strong argument because it focuses on the heart of the faith rather than a few verses, and it matches the equal treatment required by UK law since 2014.

On the other hand, many believers disagree. The Catholic Church, Orthodox Jews and many Evangelicals teach that marriage was created by God between a man and a woman: 'a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife' (Genesis 2:24), and Jesus repeated this in Matthew 19. They argue marriage should be open to children, which a same-sex couple cannot naturally achieve, and that Leviticus 18:22 forbids same-sex acts. The Church of England still teaches marriage is between a man and a woman, although it now blesses same-sex couples. This argument is strong for those who see scripture and tradition as fixed, but weaker for those who note that many couples who cannot have children still marry.

In conclusion, I think the statement is partly true. Religious believers should certainly accept gay people with respect, as even the Catholic Catechism teaches. However, 'accept same-sex marriage' asks believers to change their understanding of a sacrament, and they are free to disagree under UK law. Because both sides use serious religious arguments, I judge that the liberal view is more consistent with the command to love, but the traditional view is a reasonable reading of scripture.

exam.conclusion: Believers should respect gay people, but whether they accept same-sex marriage depends on how they read scripture. The liberal argument from love is strong, but the traditional view is a sincere reading that the law protects.

A different belief, held by Orthodox Jews, is that having different roles for men and women in worship is not discrimination. This is because they believe men and women are equal in value but God gave them different duties, so separate seating and male rabbis are a sign of difference, not unfairness.
points: Church of England, liberal Christian or Reform Jewish: all gender discrimination is wrong, including in religious roles (1), Genesis 1:27 / Galatians 3:28 / women priests and rabbis (1).
Catholic, conservative Evangelical or Orthodox Jewish: different roles are not discrimination (1), equal value but different God-given duties / male apostles / Mishnah Kiddushin 1:7 (1).

exam.q: 'Religion does more to cause gender prejudice than to challenge it.' Evaluate this statement. In your answer you: should give reasoned arguments in support of this statement; should give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view; should refer to religious arguments; may refer to non-religious arguments; should reach a justified conclusion.
exam.model:
Some people agree with this statement. They point out that many religions limit what women can do: the Catholic Church only ordains men, Orthodox synagogues have male rabbis and separate seating, and some Christians quote Paul, 'Women should remain silent in the churches' (1 Corinthians 14:34). Humanists argue that when religious leaders teach that men should lead and women should submit (Ephesians 5:22), this can shape attitudes at home and at work, and that the Equality Act 2010 even gives religions an exemption to keep male-only clergy. This argument is strong because it uses real examples, but it can treat 'different roles' as prejudice when believers sincerely see them as equal in value.

On the other hand, religion has also been a powerful force against gender prejudice. Christians and Jews teach that 'God created mankind in his own image... male and female' (Genesis 1:27), so both sexes have equal worth. Jesus broke the customs of his day by teaching women and appearing first to them after the resurrection, and Paul wrote that in Christ 'there is neither... male and female' (Galatians 3:28). The Church of England has ordained women since 1994 and installed Sarah Mullally as Archbishop of Canterbury in 2026; Reform Judaism has had women rabbis in Britain since 1975; and Christian charities such as Tearfund campaign for girls' education worldwide. This argument is strong because it shows religion changing society and itself, using its own core teachings.

In conclusion, I disagree with the statement. Some religious practices have supported unequal treatment, and that criticism should be taken seriously. However, the central religious teaching that every person is made in God's image is one of the strongest foundations for equality, and many believers have used it to challenge sexism. Overall, religion seems to do more to challenge gender prejudice than to cause it, even if it is not always consistent.
for: Male-only priesthood (Catholic) and male rabbis and separate seating (Orthodox Judaism).
Texts such as 1 Corinthians 14:34, 1 Timothy 2:12 and Ephesians 5:22 have been used to limit women.
Religious exemptions in the Equality Act 2010.
Humanist argument: traditional teaching can shape sexist attitudes in society.
Evaluation: strong examples, but may mistake 'different roles' for prejudice.
against: Genesis 1:27: male and female both in God's image; Galatians 3:28: all one in Christ.
Jesus' respect for women (Luke 10:38-42; first resurrection witnesses).
Women priests (1994), bishops (2015) and Archbishop of Canterbury (2026); women rabbis since 1975.
Christian charities such as Tearfund and Christian Aid support women and girls.
Evaluation: strong because it shows religion's core teachings driving change.
exam.conclusion: Some religious practices have supported unequal treatment, but the teaching that all are made in God's image has been a powerful basis for challenging sexism, so religion does more to challenge gender prejudice than to cause it.

truefalse.s: Adultery means having sex before you are married.
truefalse.why: Adultery is sex where at least one person is married to someone else. Sex before marriage is a different issue.

truefalse.s: The Catholic Church teaches that being gay is not in itself a sin.
truefalse.why: It teaches that homosexual acts are wrong, but the orientation is not a sin, and gay people must be respected.

truefalse.s: As of 2026, Church of England priests can conduct same-sex weddings.
truefalse.why: They cannot. Since 2023 same-sex couples can receive Prayers of Love and Faith blessings in ordinary services.

truefalse.s: Judaism teaches that sex within marriage is good and holy, not only for having children.
truefalse.why: Jewish teaching values sexual pleasure and closeness in marriage, as well as procreation.

truefalse.s: Humanists think sex before marriage is always wrong.
truefalse.why: Humanists judge relationships by consent, honesty, respect and avoiding harm, not by marital status.

truefalse.s: The contraceptive pill works by causing an abortion.
truefalse.why: It mainly stops ovulation, so no egg is fertilised. Examiners say this is a common error.

truefalse.s: The Catholic Church allows natural family planning for serious reasons.
truefalse.why: It works with the body's natural cycle, so the Church accepts it.

truefalse.s: The Church of England first accepted contraception at the Lambeth Conference of 1930.
truefalse.why: Resolution 15 accepted other methods for good moral reasons.

truefalse.s: Orthodox Jews generally allow contraception for any reason the couple chooses.
truefalse.why: Orthodox Jews usually allow it only for serious reasons such as the mother's health. Reform Jews leave it to the couple.

truefalse.s: Catholics teach that the only purpose of sex is to have children.
truefalse.why: They teach it is unitive (love) and procreative, but each act must remain open to new life.

truefalse.s: The words 'till death us do part' are a quotation from the Bible.
truefalse.why: They come from the Christian wedding service, not the Bible.

truefalse.s: Quakers, Methodists and the United Reformed Church hold same-sex weddings.
truefalse.why: Quakers from 2014, the URC since 2016 and the Methodist Church since 2021.

truefalse.s: Couples who live together for many years have a 'common law marriage' in England and Wales.
truefalse.why: There is no such thing in English law, so cohabiting couples have fewer rights.

truefalse.s: Catholics believe marriage is a sacrament.
truefalse.why: It is one of the seven sacraments and is lifelong.

truefalse.s: Humanist weddings are legally recognised in Scotland.
truefalse.why: Since 2005. As of November 2026 they are not yet legally recognised in England and Wales.

truefalse.s: An annulment is the Catholic name for a divorce.
truefalse.why: An annulment says a valid sacramental marriage never existed. It is not the ending of a valid marriage.

truefalse.s: Jesus allowed divorce in the case of sexual immorality (Matthew 19:9).
truefalse.why: This exception is used by many Protestants to accept divorce in some cases.

truefalse.s: Since 2022, a person in England and Wales must prove their partner's fault to get divorced.
truefalse.why: No-fault divorce means a statement that the marriage has broken down is enough.

truefalse.s: In Judaism, divorce is allowed, although it is seen as sad.
truefalse.why: Deuteronomy 24:1 allows a get, and the Talmud says the altar sheds tears.

truefalse.s: The Church of England never allows divorced people to remarry in church.
truefalse.why: Since 2002 they may, at the priest's discretion.

truefalse.s: An extended family includes relatives such as grandparents, aunts and uncles.
truefalse.why: A nuclear family is parents and children; an extended family adds other relatives.

truefalse.s: Polygamy is legal in the UK if all partners agree.
truefalse.why: Marrying while already married (bigamy) is a crime in the UK.

truefalse.s: Educating children in a faith is one of the purposes of the family named by AQA.
truefalse.why: The others are procreation and stability and protection of children.

truefalse.s: Jews today follow the polygamy of Abraham and Jacob.
truefalse.why: A ruling by Rabbenu Gershom around 1000 CE banned it for Ashkenazi Jews, and Jews today are monogamous.

truefalse.s: All Christians oppose same-sex couples raising children.
truefalse.why: Catholics prefer a mother and father, but many Protestants and Quakers say love and care matter most.

truefalse.s: The Church of England has ordained women as bishops since 2015.
truefalse.why: Libby Lane was the first, in January 2015.

truefalse.s: Orthodox Jews teach that women are of less value than men.
truefalse.why: They teach that men and women are equal in value but have different roles.

truefalse.s: In Reform Judaism women can be rabbis and are counted in a minyan.
truefalse.why: Reform and Liberal Judaism practise full equality in worship.

truefalse.s: The Catholic Church ordains women as priests.
truefalse.why: Only men are ordained, following Jesus' choice of twelve male apostles.

truefalse.s: Discrimination is an action, while prejudice is an attitude.
truefalse.why: Prejudice is what you think; discrimination is what you do.

truefalse.s: Paying a woman less than a man for the same work is legal in the UK.
truefalse.why: It has been illegal since the Equal Pay Act 1970 and is covered by the Equality Act 2010.

truefalse.s: All religious believers agree that men-only priesthood is discrimination.
truefalse.why: Catholics and Orthodox Jews say different roles are not discrimination; liberal believers disagree.

truefalse.s: Christians use the Golden Rule to argue against gender prejudice.
truefalse.why: 'Do to others what you would have them do to you' (Matthew 7:12).

short.q: Give one religious belief about human sexuality.
short.a: Sex is a gift from God for marriage (accept: for love and procreation; heterosexual relationships are God's plan; same-sex relationships can be loving and accepted).

short.q: Give one reason why some Christians believe sex before marriage is wrong.
short.a: Sex is meant for the lifelong commitment of marriage (accept: 1 Corinthians 6:18 'flee from sexual immorality'; it could lead to an unplanned pregnancy outside a stable family).

short.q: Name one Christian denomination that holds same-sex weddings.
short.a: Quakers (accept: Methodist Church; United Reformed Church).

short.q: Give the meaning of the term 'adultery'.
short.a: Sex between two people where at least one is married to someone else.

short.q: Give one example of artificial contraception.
short.a: The pill (accept: condom, implant, coil, injection, sterilisation).

short.q: Name the 1968 Catholic document that rejected artificial contraception.
short.a: Humanae Vitae.

short.q: Give one reason why some religious believers accept contraception within marriage.
short.a: To plan a family responsibly (accept: to protect the mother's health; money reasons; to care for existing children).

short.q: Give one natural method of family planning.
short.a: The rhythm method (accept: natural family planning; avoiding sex at fertile times).

short.q: Give one religious purpose of marriage.
short.a: Companionship (accept: having children; a safe place for sex; raising children in the faith; stability).

short.q: Give the meaning of the term 'cohabitation'.
short.a: A couple living together without being married or in a civil partnership.

short.q: Name the canopy under which a Jewish couple marry.
short.a: Chuppah.

short.q: Give one reason why some religious believers oppose same-sex marriage.
short.a: They believe marriage is between a man and a woman (accept: Genesis 2:24; marriage should be open to children; Leviticus 18:22).

short.q: Give one reason why some religious believers accept remarriage.
short.a: God forgives and everyone deserves a second chance (accept: Jesus allowed divorce for adultery; companionship; to give children a stable home).

short.q: Name the Jewish document of divorce.
short.a: A get.

short.q: Give one ethical argument used against divorce.
short.a: The sanctity of marriage vows (accept: promises made before God must be kept; harm to children).

short.q: Give one common reason for divorce.
short.a: Adultery (accept: domestic abuse, growing apart, money problems, addiction).

short.q: Give one religious belief about the nature of the family.
short.a: The family is based on marriage (accept: created by God; includes caring for elderly parents; extended family).

short.q: Give one role of children in a religious family.
short.a: To honour their parents (accept: obey parents; care for them in old age; learn and practise the faith).

short.q: Give one reason why many religious believers do not support polygamy.
short.a: Marriage is between two people, 'one flesh' (accept: 1 Corinthians 7:2; it is unfair or causes jealousy; it is illegal in the UK).

short.q: Give the meaning of the term 'nuclear family'.
short.a: Two parents and their children living together.

short.q: Name one Christian denomination that ordains women.
short.a: Church of England (accept: Methodist Church; Salvation Army; United Reformed Church).

short.q: Give one Bible verse used to support gender equality.
short.a: Genesis 1:27 (accept: Galatians 3:28; Ephesians 5:21).

short.q: Give the meaning of the term 'minyan'.
short.a: The group of ten Jewish adults needed for certain prayers (in Orthodox Judaism, ten men).

short.q: Give one example of gender discrimination.
short.a: Paying a woman less than a man for the same job (accept: refusing a job or promotion because of sex; sacking a pregnant woman).

short.q: Give one religious teaching which shows gender prejudice is wrong.
short.a: All are made in God's image, Genesis 1:27 (accept: Galatians 3:28; Matthew 7:12; love your neighbour).

short.q: Name the UK law that makes sex discrimination illegal.
short.a: The Equality Act 2010 (accept: Sex Discrimination Act 1975; Equal Pay Act 1970).
